title: SQL Dates and Date/Time Values

understand.concept: Date and time values represent calendar dates, clock times or instants. SQL products use different date/time types and functions. SQLite has no dedicated DATE or DATETIME storage class; applications commonly store ISO-8601 text, Julian day numbers or Unix timestamps and use date(), time(), datetime(), julianday() and strftime().
understand.whyItMatters: Correct date handling is essential for billing, scheduling, reports, ordering events and calculating durations. Consistent formats and time-zone rules prevent subtle errors.

explain.narrative:
## Date and time are not one universal type
SQL Server offers types such as date, time, datetime2 and datetimeoffset; MySQL and PostgreSQL have their own date/time types and functions. SQLite has no dedicated date/time storage class. It accepts supported ISO-8601 text, Julian day numbers and Unix timestamps as time-values.

## SQLite date/time functions
Use date() for a date string, time() for a time, datetime() for a combined value, julianday() for numeric day calculations and strftime() for formatted parts. Modifiers such as '+7 days' transform a time-value. Use UTC or a clearly defined time-zone strategy for instants; local civil time can change with daylight-saving rules.

## Good practice
Prefer unambiguous ISO-8601 values, avoid locale-dependent strings, document whether a value is UTC or local time, and test boundary cases such as month ends and leap days. Do not assume SQLite's functions and another DBMS's DATEADD/DATEDIFF syntax are interchangeable.

questions.prompt: Which statement about SQLite date/time storage is correct?
options: SQLite has no dedicated DATE storage class
SQLite stores every date only as a native DATE type
SQLite stores dates only as local time
questions.answer: SQLite has no dedicated DATE storage class
questions.explanation: SQLite uses supported text, Julian day or Unix timestamp representations.

questions.prompt: Which SQLite function returns a date string?
questions.explanation: date() is a built-in SQLite date/time function.

questions.prompt: What is a safe, unambiguous text date format?
questions.explanation: ISO-style year-month-day avoids many locale ambiguities.

questions.prompt: Why should applications document UTC versus local time?
options: The same wall-clock time can mean different instants across zones and transitions
questions.answer: The same wall-clock time can mean different instants across zones and transitions
questions.explanation: Time-zone policy is part of correct timestamp interpretation.
Julian day numbers support date/time arithmetic.
